title: "OpenTelemetry"
description: "Export traces, metrics, and logs to an OTLP collector and tag them per turn."

# OpenTelemetry

Agent SDK sends traces, metrics, and logs to an OTLP collector when you
set the `OTEL_*` variables. Record your own with `@opentelemetry/api`.

```bash
export OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=https://otel.example.com
export OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS="Authorization=Bearer%20$OTEL_TOKEN"
export OTEL_SERVICE_NAME=incident-agent
agent-sdk serve --dir . --dev
```

- The default protocol is `http/protobuf`. `http/json` also works, and
  `grpc` logs a warning and falls back to `http/protobuf`.
- Metrics use delta temporality. Grafana Cloud and Prometheus reject
  delta, so set `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_METRICS_TEMPORALITY_PREFERENCE=cumulative`
  when you export to either one.
- If you don't set an endpoint, Agent SDK doesn't export anything.
- You can create a meter, tracer, or logger at the top of
  `bot/agent.ts`, and it will use Agent SDK's providers.

## Variables

| Variable | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` | Base URL. Appends `/v1/traces`, `/v1/metrics`, `/v1/logs`. |
| `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT` | Traces URL, used as written. Overrides the base URL. |
| `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_METRICS_ENDPOINT` | Metrics URL, used as written. Overrides the base URL. |
| `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_LOGS_ENDPOINT` | Logs URL, used as written. Overrides the base URL. |
| `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS` | Sent on every export. URL-encode values. Reread on each export. |
| `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL` | `http/protobuf` (default) or `http/json`. |
| `OTEL_SERVICE_NAME` | `service.name`. Defaults to the agent name, then `unknown_service:node`. |
| `OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES` | `service.namespace`, `service.version`, `deployment.environment.name`. |
| `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_METRICS_TEMPORALITY_PREFERENCE` | `delta` (default), `cumulative`, or `lowmemory`. |
| `OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER` | `otlp` exports logs. Unset, `none`, and `console` do not. |
| `OTEL_SDK_DISABLED` | `true` turns export off. |
| `OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER` | `none` turns traces off. |
| `OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER` | `none` turns metrics off. |
| `OTEL_LOG_USER_PROMPTS` | `1` adds prompt text to log records. |
| `OTEL_LOG_TOOL_CONTENT` | `1` adds tool payloads to log records. |
| `AGENT_SDK_OTEL_SEMCONV` | Trace format: `legacy` (default), `standard`, or `both`. See [Trace format](#trace-format). |
| `OTEL_INSTRUMENTATION_GENAI_CAPTURE_MESSAGE_CONTENT` | `true` or `span_only` adds prompts, replies, and tool payloads to `standard` and `both` spans. |

## Trace format

By default, Agent SDK names its spans `agent_sdk.turn`, `agent_sdk.tool`,
and `agent_sdk.subagent`, and keys them with `agent_sdk.*` and `cursor.*`
attributes. Observability tools that read the
[OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions](https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai)
don't recognize those names. Set `AGENT_SDK_OTEL_SEMCONV` to send spans
they can map without a custom mapper.

| Value | Span names | Attributes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `legacy` (default) | `agent_sdk.turn`, `agent_sdk.tool`, `agent_sdk.subagent` | `agent_sdk.*` and `cursor.*`, unchanged |
| `standard` | `invoke_agent <agent>`, `execute_tool <tool>`, `invoke_agent <subagent>` | `gen_ai.*` where a GenAI key exists, `agent_sdk.*` for the rest |
| `both` | Same as `legacy` | Every `legacy` and every `standard` key |

An unknown value logs a warning and keeps `legacy`.

The format changes turn, tool, and subagent spans, and the conversation id
key on spans you start during a turn. Turn phase spans keep their
`agent_sdk.turn.<phase>` names. Span events, HTTP and MCP spans, metrics,
and log records are the same in every format.

### Attribute mapping

| `legacy` | `standard` | Span |
| --- | --- | --- |
| (none) | `gen_ai.operation.name`: `invoke_agent` or `execute_tool` | turn, subagent, tool |
| `cursor.conversation.id`, `agent_sdk.session_id` | `gen_ai.conversation.id` | all |
| `agent_sdk.agent` | `gen_ai.agent.name` | turn, tool |
| `agent_sdk.subagent_name` | `gen_ai.agent.name` | subagent |
| `agent_sdk.subagent_description` | `gen_ai.agent.description` | subagent |
| (none) | `gen_ai.request.model` | turn |
| `agent_sdk.finish_reason` on `message.completed` events | `gen_ai.response.finish_reasons` | turn |
| `agent_sdk.usage.input_tokens` | `gen_ai.usage.input_tokens` | turn |
| `agent_sdk.usage.output_tokens` | `gen_ai.usage.output_tokens` | turn |
| `agent_sdk.usage.cache_read_tokens` | `gen_ai.usage.cache_read.input_tokens` | turn |
| `agent_sdk.usage.cache_write_tokens` | `gen_ai.usage.cache_creation.input_tokens` | turn |
| `agent_sdk.usage.reasoning_tokens` | `gen_ai.usage.reasoning.output_tokens` | turn |
| `cursor.tool.name` | `gen_ai.tool.name` | tool |
| `agent_sdk.call_id` | `gen_ai.tool.call.id` | tool |
| `agent_sdk.tool_args` | `gen_ai.tool.call.arguments` | tool |
| `agent_sdk.tool_output` | `gen_ai.tool.call.result` | tool |
| `agent_sdk.tool_error_class` | `error.type` | tool |
| `cursor.tool.status`, `cursor.tool.kind` | Dropped. A failed tool has `error.type` and an error status. | tool |

Every other attribute keeps its name. `gen_ai.input.messages`,
`gen_ai.output.messages`, `gen_ai.request.model`,
`gen_ai.response.finish_reasons`, and `error.type` appear only in
`standard` and `both`.

Your trace tags follow the same table in `standard` and `both`. A tag
that names the conversation, the agent, the turn, or the tool call is
dropped so it can't replace the runtime's value: `cursor.conversation.id`,
`agent_sdk.session_id`, `agent_sdk.agent`, `agent_sdk.subagent_name`,
`agent_sdk.turn_id`, `agent_sdk.call_id`, `cursor.tool.name`, and their
`gen_ai.*` counterparts. In `legacy`, trace tags are copied as written.

`error.type` is a short class on any span that ends in error:

- On a turn, the runner's error code, `cancelled`, or `_OTHER`.
- On a tool, `auth_required`, `denied`, `not_found`, `rate_limited`,
  `timeout`, `unauthorized`, or `tool_error`, and `incomplete` when the
  turn ended before the tool returned.
- On a subagent, `_OTHER`, or `incomplete` when the turn ended first.

`gen_ai.request.model` is the model the turn asked for. A model fallback
doesn't change it.

### Message content

Spans carry no prompts, replies, or tool payloads unless you opt in, in
any format.

| Setting | `legacy` | `standard` and `both` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `OTEL_INSTRUMENTATION_GENAI_CAPTURE_MESSAGE_CONTENT=true` | Nothing | `gen_ai.input.messages`, `gen_ai.output.messages`, `gen_ai.tool.call.arguments`, `gen_ai.tool.call.result`, `gen_ai.agent.description` |
| `OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER=otlp` and `OTEL_LOG_USER_PROMPTS=1` | Log records only | Also `gen_ai.input.messages` |
| `OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER=otlp` and `OTEL_LOG_TOOL_CONTENT=1` | `agent_sdk.tool_args`, `agent_sdk.tool_output` | The same payloads under the keys of the format |

`span_only` and `span_and_event` work like `true`. `false`, `no_content`,
and `event_only` add nothing, because Agent SDK doesn't emit GenAI events.
`gen_ai.input.messages` holds the turn's user prompts, and
`gen_ai.output.messages` holds its final reply. Agent SDK cuts each text
to 2,048 characters. `gen_ai.tool.call.arguments` and
`gen_ai.tool.call.result` hold the payload as JSON. A payload longer than
2,048 characters becomes a JSON string of its first 2,048 characters, so
every value still parses.

### Move a dashboard to standard

1. Set `AGENT_SDK_OTEL_SEMCONV=both` and redeploy. Existing dashboards keep
   working, and every span gains its `gen_ai.*` keys.
2. Rewrite queries with the mapping table, for example
   `cursor.conversation.id` to `gen_ai.conversation.id`, and connect your
   vendor's GenAI view.
3. Queries on span names don't move in `both`. In `standard`, filter on
   `gen_ai.operation.name` instead of `agent_sdk.turn` or `agent_sdk.tool`.
4. Set `AGENT_SDK_OTEL_SEMCONV=standard` once nothing reads the legacy keys.

On a hosted agent, add `AGENT_SDK_OTEL_SEMCONV` to `hosting.secretNames`
and set it with `agent-sdk secret set` like the other variables.

## Hosted agents

```ts
export default defineAgent({
  hosting: {
    egressDomains: ["otlp-gateway-prod-us-east-0.grafana.net"],
    secretNames: [
      "OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT",
      "OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS",
      "OTEL_SERVICE_NAME",
    ],
  },
});
```

`service.name` is fixed by the first export, so redeploy to change it.

## Record and tag

```ts
import { metrics, trace } from "@opentelemetry/api";
import { logs } from "@opentelemetry/api-logs";
import { currentConversationId } from "@grok/agent-sdk/otel";

const tracer = trace.getTracer("incident-agent");
const lookups = metrics.getMeter("incident-agent").createCounter("incident.lookups");
const logger = logs.getLogger("incident-agent");

lookups.add(1, { "cursor.conversation.id": currentConversationId() });
```

Spans started during a turn get `cursor.conversation.id`
(`gen_ai.conversation.id` in the `standard` trace format, both keys in
`both`), and a metric gets it only when you set it.

To tag a whole turn, call `ctx.telemetry` from a tool. Spans in the
turn get the trace keys, Agent SDK's log records get the log keys, and
`cursor.token.usage` gets the metric keys. Outside a tool, use
`telemetry` from `@grok/agent-sdk/telemetry`.

```ts
async execute({ key }, ctx) {
  ctx.telemetry.setTraceAttributes({ "work.item": key });
  ctx.telemetry.setMetricAttributes({ "work.item": key });
  ctx.telemetry.setLogAttributes({ "work.item": key });
  return await jira.getIssue(key);
}
```

Grafana renames a `.` in a metric key to `_`.

```promql
sum by (work_item) (cursor_token_usage_total)
```

- Each distinct metric value is a new series, so never use a per-turn
  ID, a secret, an email, or a raw user ID.
- A session holds up to 32 keys of each kind, with keys up to 128
  characters and values up to 256.

## Limits

- Agent SDK doesn't support custom span processors, samplers, views,
  your own OpenTelemetry SDK, or library auto-instrumentation. It reads
  `OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER` and `OTEL_METRIC_EXPORT_INTERVAL` once at
  startup, so restart the process after you change either one.
- Import Agent SDK before any other OpenTelemetry setup. Otherwise the
  turn's tags may not reach your spans.

## Migrating from serve({ otel })

Delete `serve({ otel })`, `bot/otel.ts`, `bot/instrumentation.ts`, and
any `defineOtel` call. Set these variables instead.

| Old option | Set this instead |
| --- | --- |
| `serviceName` | `OTEL_SERVICE_NAME` |
| `serviceVersion` | `service.version` in `OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES` |
| `resourceAttributes` | `OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES`, comma-separated, URL-encoded values |
| `exporters[].url` | `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` (appends `/v1/traces`, `/v1/metrics`, `/v1/logs`) |
| `exporters[].url` with `signals` | `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT`, `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_METRICS_ENDPOINT`, or `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_LOGS_ENDPOINT`, used as written |
| `exporters[].headers` | `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS`, comma-separated, URL-encoded values |
| `exporters[].protocol` | `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL`, or `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_PROTOCOL`, `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_METRICS_PROTOCOL`, `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_LOGS_PROTOCOL` |
| `exporters[].signals` | The per-signal URL. `OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER=none`, `OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER=none`, or `OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER=none` stops that signal. |
| `traces: false` | `OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER=none` |
| `traces: true` | Leave `OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER` unset. Traces start when an endpoint is set. |
| `traces.sampleRatio` | `OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER=parentbased_traceidratio` and `OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER_ARG`, before process start |
| `metrics: false` | `OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER=none` |
| `metrics: true` | Leave `OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER` unset. Metrics start when a metrics URL is set. |
| `metrics.exportIntervalMillis` | `OTEL_METRIC_EXPORT_INTERVAL`, milliseconds, before process start |
| `logs: false` | Unset `OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER`, or set `none` |
| `logs: true` | `OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER=otlp` |
| `logs.userPrompts` | `OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER=otlp` and `OTEL_LOG_USER_PROMPTS=1` |
| `logs.toolContent` | `OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER=otlp` and `OTEL_LOG_TOOL_CONTENT=1` |
| `otel: false` | No endpoint, or `OTEL_SDK_DISABLED=true` |

Set the hosted values after deploy:

```bash
agent-sdk secret set my-agent OTEL_SERVICE_NAME OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS
```
